title: Talking with Protestants
tagline: A charitable course on the big questions between Catholics and Protestants, with their best case heard first.
whyItMatters: Protestants are our fellow Christians, and the conversation is usually about the Bible, grace and the Church. A friend who has listened and read their sources can speak with truth and kindness.

mindset.tip: Be gentle and respectful, and ask what they mean by "saved", "Bible alone" or "the Church" before you answer. (1 Peter 3:15-16)
Begin with what we share: baptism, the Creed, love of Christ and of Scripture. The Church calls other baptized Christians brothers and sisters. (CCC 818-819; Unitatis Redintegratio 3)
Read the Protestant confessions yourself, so that you answer what they really hold and not a caricature.
Be honest that sins on both sides led to division, and that real abuses needed reform. (CCC 817)
Take one question at a time, and pray for unity: it needs conversion of heart, not only good arguments. (CCC 821)
